How it works

1. Automated test (node scripts/snippet-qa.mjs): runs each snippet in headless Chrome. On desktop it records JS errors, failed loads, blank renders and broken images. It clicks, types into and changes every control, and notes which ones change nothing. Games get a keyboard check and scroll effects a scroll check. At 390px it checks for sideways scrolling and small tap targets. It also flags low-contrast or tiny text, unnamed buttons, unlabelled inputs, missing focus styles and missing reduced-motion support. Only new or changed snippets are retested; --limit=200 runs a batch, --category=games one category, --force everything.

SEO content (checked on every rebuild, all snippets): title 50–60 chars (max 60), meta description 150–160 (max 160), duplicate titles, thin About text, missing or few How-to steps, features, use cases and FAQs, links to snippets that don't exist, and write-ups that name functions, classes or constants the code doesn't have (a sign the description went stale after an edit).

2. Manual review: snippets are opened and checked by hand in batches, and the verdicts go into snippet-qa/review.json. Manual notes replace the auto text in the Functionality and Look & feel columns.

3. Fix: snippets marked Needs work or Broken get fixed and marked Fixed, then retested.

What the checks can't catch, so the manual review still matters: logic that runs without errors but gives the wrong result (wrong maths, a game rule that's off, walls drawn on the wrong side), whether a design actually looks good, copy that is accurate but unhelpful, and effects that only show over time or on real touch devices. The auto results tell us where to look first; the review decides.

Rebuild this page without testing: node scripts/snippet-qa-report.mjs. The auto checks are heuristics: a "control changed nothing" can be a control whose effect is only visual over time, so always confirm by hand before fixing.
